newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sichuan Instrument sets up nuclear tool line.
newsitem.headline: Sichuan Instrument sets up nuclear tool line.

text.p: Sichuan Instrument Co Ltd has completed a production line to turn out precision instruments used in nuclear power plants to be exported to Iran and Pakistan, the China Securities Bulletin said on Thursday.

A report earlier this week in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said completion of the 40 million yuan project marked Sichuan Instrument as a pioneer in China's efforts to produce its own nuclear plant components.

The project should become one of the firm's chief sources of profits over the next several years, the bulletin quoted a company spokesman as saying. The product was expected to generate net earnings of about 10 million yuan annually, he said.
"Most of the nuclear instruments are slated for export to such countries as Pakistan and Iran," the bulletin quoted the spokesman as saying.
The exports were part of China's long-standing policy of assisting developing countries, he said.
A small proportion of the instruments would be supplied to China's Qinshan nuclear power station in eastern Zhejiang province, he said.

Power plant control instruments produced by the Shenzhen-listed company had been certified as "accurate and reliable" by industry experts, said the Securities Times without specifying who made the assessment.
A specialist in the nuclear power sector said Sichuan Instrument's gauges would be used in nuclear island control systems, which contain the plant's reactor.
Sichuan Instrument spent more than three years to set up and refine the instrument production line, the newspaper said.

Sichuan Instrument, which mainly produces instruments for use in the power, petrochemical and metal industries, said it has forecast net earnings of 33.78 million yuan for this year, compared with 20.74 million yuan in 1995.
The company said it notched up net earnings of 16.68 million yuan in the January-June period of 1996.
